verdict.rationale: Supabase's RLS system and API-key model (docs-4, docs-15) provide a mechanism for scoped, least-privilege access, and the MCP integration docs (supabase-docs-1/27) frame agent access as project-scoped. However, a documented real-world incident shows the Cursor+Supabase MCP agent operated with the full-access service_role key, bypassing RLS entirely and leaking sensitive data (supabase-comm-1), directly contradicting the least-privilege claim; Supabase's own engineer response (supabase-comm-3) confirms they had to retroactively default MCP to read-only as a mitigation, acknowledging the gap. missing for 10: evidence of a dedicated agent-specific credential/token scoping mechanism (e.g., granular MCP API keys or per-agent RLS policies) rather than reliance on generic RLS/service-role keys, and confirmation the read-only default fully closes the least-privilege gap.
